correctness.rationale: Every rank-at-most-d correlation matrix is represented by unit normals in \(\mathbb R^d\), and for fixed normals the event at threshold \(t\) is the dilation \(tK\). Gaussian density convergence at the origin gives the fixed-configuration asymptotic. The nontrivial uniform lower bound is handled by truncating \(K\) in a ball: compactness of the normal configuration space and boundary-null continuity give minima \(a_R\), and monotone exhaustion forces \(a_R\uparrow V_{d,n}\); otherwise a convergent sequence of minimizers would produce a limiting polyhedron of full volume below \(V_{d,n}\). This controls even \(t\)-dependent near-minimizers. In three dimensions with five facets, the minimum-volume unit-inradius circumscribed polyhedron is the right equilateral triangular prism; its cross-section has side \(2\sqrt3\), area \(3\sqrt3\), and height two, hence volume \(6\sqrt3\).
risks: The theorem is asymptotic as \(t\downarrow0\); it does not identify the exact minimizer for any fixed positive threshold.

originality.rationale: Mulgund's current primary paper explicitly poses the fixed-threshold rank-constrained problem for \(d\ge3,n\ge d+2\) and states that outside a few special cases the optimal configurations are unknown. The triangular-prism tangent-volume fact itself is classical, so it is not counted as new. The surviving contribution is the general small-threshold reduction, including the uniformity over varying covariance configurations, and its consequence that the first open \((d,n)=(3,5)\) case has a rigorous leading constant.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a structural reduction of a current Gaussian extremal problem to a natural Euclidean tangent-polyhedron invariant. It also resolves the leading-order behavior of the first three-dimensional five-direction case left open at fixed threshold, with an exact constant.
risks: It is a leading-order boundary theorem, not the full fixed-threshold solution.

final_claim: For centered Gaussian vectors with unit marginal variances and covariance rank at most \(d\), the minimum common-threshold probability among \(n\) coordinates has the small-positive-threshold asymptotic \(m_{d,n}(t)\sim (2\pi)^{-d/2}V_{d,n}t^d\), where \(V_{d,n}\) is the minimum volume of an origin-centered unit-inradius polyhedron cut out by \(n\) unit halfspaces. In particular, \(V_{3,5}=6\sqrt3\), attained by the right equilateral triangular prism.
limitations: Unit marginal variances and covariance rank at most \(d\).
The prism statement gives the leading asymptotic, not an exact optimizer for every positive threshold.
